findings.claim: The Redis session store TTL is 600 seconds and the cookie has no maxAge, so connect-redis uses the store ttl and server-side sessions expire after 10 minutes of inactivity.
findings.would_refute: A cookie maxAge or expires being set (connect-redis then derives the TTL from the cookie)

findings.claim: The canary deployment reads SESSION_SECRET from a different Kubernetes secret than the stable deployment, and the Service routes to both, so a session signed by one pod fails verification on the other.
findings.would_refute: Both secrets containing the same session-secret value

findings.claim: rolling is false. That only controls re-sending the cookie; express-session still touches the store on every request, so it is not why sessions expire.
findings.would_refute: rolling: true in the session options
